**Finding: deviation (high severity) — Rule T4C, Termination for convenience**

**What the document does:** Section 6(a) allows either party to terminate for any or no reason on 15 days' notice, but *only* "[a]t any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding." The sole other exit, Section 6(b), requires an uncured material breach. Section 2 makes the term evergreen — it runs until terminated under Paragraph 6.

**Why it fails:** Since Statements of Work are the vehicle for all Services, we have no convenience right whenever work is actually underway, on an agreement of indefinite duration. That misses both the preferred position (30 days' notice with pro-rata refund) and the fallback (60–90 days' notice), and falls into walk-away territory.

**What I did not flag:** RadialSpark's 15-day convenience right in 6(a) is exercisable only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so there is no live engagement it can abandon — short of the fallback's "90 days at end of term," but not materially harmful to us, and noted rather than redlined.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** new Section 6(c) giving Clear Capital a 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any Statement of Work, with no penalty or forfeiture, payment limited to Services actually performed, refund of prepaid fees, and assignment of works in progress.
